text:
deploy-bot: finished rollout: adaptive-microbatch-scheduler v2 -> prod (hash: d4c3f2). config: auto-scale microbatching + kernel-fallbacks enabled :rocket:

sagar: seeing p99 jump on model-a across us-west-2, looks like +140ms since deploy :eyes:

mira: confirming, p50 stable but tail moved. Datadog trace: https://dd.example.com/graph/xyz (screenshot in thread)

noah: quick profiler dump shows higher time in kernel selection path, lots of `choose_kernel()` calls and more `conv_to_fp16` conversions. stack sample:```
choose_kernel(model_a, seq=1024) -> best_kernel=matmul_opt_v3
matmul_opt_v3 -> fallback path triggers quant_dequant on first token
kv_cache.miss++
```

jin: config diff from canary -> prod:```
- microbatch.max_items: 64
+ microbatch.max_items: 128
- kernel_selection.policy: stable
+ kernel_selection.policy: latency_aware
- kv_cache.prefetch: true
+ kv_cache.prefetch: false
```

emily: suspecting microbatch sizing + changed kernel policy increased first-token setup cost and disabled prefetch -> more KV misses -> tail. p99 heatmap shows correlation with larger batch windows.

sagar: rolling rollback plan? we can revert only the microbatch sizing quickly via flag, or full rollback of scheduler. Which is faster?

mira: toggle microbatch.max_items back to 64 would be low-risk and immediate. kernel policy revert needs model warmup in canary first.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1785, pager: on-call notified.

noah: quick sanity check: can we flip `kv_cache.prefetch: true` in prod? That will reduce misses but might increase memory. We should check memory headroom.

emily: memory headroom ~18% on the pool nodes. prefetch true seems safe for short-term. But microbatch revert is less intrusive.

sagar: executing change: ```sh
# toggling feature flag via runtime-config
runtimectl set model_a.microbatch.max_items=64 --env=prod --reason="p99 spike after v2"
```

deploy-bot: config change applied (id: cfg-7782). rolling update to runtime pools started.

mira: graph is already showing p99 dropping on a subset of nodes. keeping it under watch.

noah: recorded a flamegraph pre/post. pre-deploy had small kernel-selection overhead, post-deploy shows a red hotspot in `select_opt_kernel()` during first-token path. pushing flamegraphs to the ticket.

emily: logs show kv_cache miss rate down from 7.8% -> 1.9% after microbatch revert. p99 back to baseline within 90s on most shards.

sagar: nice. do we want to fully roll back v2 or iterate? proposal: keep kernel-fallback work in staging, re-enable prefetch by default, then re-run canary with smaller microbatch cap and full perf test (tail p99 target <200ms).

mira: +1. need a perf job that synthesizes long-context traffic with cold KV cache to validate. I'll open a perf-eval.

ops-bot: incident INC-2026-1785 resolved by config revert. downtime: none, brief risk window.

jin: action items: (1) revert commit for microbatch default in infra branch (PR #3421), (2) enable kv_cache.prefetch default, (3) add perf job for cold-kv, long-seq. I'll draft PRs.

emily: add a Grafana alert for kernel-selection latency > 80ms per-request and kv_cache.miss_rate > 3% so we catch similar regressions earlier.

sagar: thanks all. postmortem to follow with perf numbers and flamegraphs. closing thread after docs + PRs. :thumbsup:
